Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testDuplicateHeaderElements()` calls `CSVFormat.DEFAULT.withHeader("A", "A").validate()` expecting an IllegalArgumentException due to duplicate header elements. From the code snippet of `CSVFormat.withHeader(String...)`, this method creates a new CSVFormat instance with the given header array (line 774). The actual validation is done in the `validate()` method. Upon inspecting the `validate()` method, particularly lines 665-671, it checks if the header array is non-null, and then checks for duplicates by converting the array into a set and comparing sizes. If duplicates are found (set size not equal to header array length), it throws an IllegalStateException with a message about duplicate names.

The test expects an IllegalArgumentException, but the code throws an IllegalStateException. Therefore, the test failure is because the code throws the wrong type of exception upon detecting duplicate headers. Also, from the current bug report, the duplicate headers should be rejected during construction (or validation), but here they are currently allowed except during a subsequent validate call that throws the wrong exception type.

Recent bug reports about duplicate columns causing inconsistencies give secondary support that duplicate headers are problematic, but they do not necessarily indicate the exception type or validation mechanics. The main problem is that duplicate headers are detected only on validate(), and with the wrong exception type.

Hence, the root cause is that the CSVFormat.validate() method throws an IllegalStateException when duplicate headers are detected, whereas the test expects an IllegalArgumentException. Also, the CSVFormat constructor or withHeader method does not currently perform any upfront duplicate checks, deferring to validate().

Summary: Duplicate headers are detected only in validate(), which throws IllegalStateException, not IllegalArgumentException as the test expects. No upfront duplicate rejection occurs in the constructor or withHeader.

Recommended fix: Validate header duplicates earlier and throw IllegalArgumentException instead of IllegalStateException for duplicates.

Relevant method for fix: CSVFormat.validate(), maybe CSVFormat.withHeader(...).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
